content.title: About
content.content: The Bologna sandwich on white bread (1813) is a classic sandwich made of sliced cooked Bologna sausage, soft cream cheese, and fresh vegetables, placed between two slices of white roll. It is popular in cafés and cafeterias as a quick, satisfying snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recipe for a Bologna sausage sandwich appeared in the early 19th century in Italy.
White bread in the original recipe is chosen without a crust to let the delicate flavor of the sausage shine.
Traditionally the sandwich includes lettuce, a tomato slice, and a light spread of mustard.
In some regions the cream cheese is replaced with mozzarella to enhance the aroma.
The sandwich is often served with potato chips or pickled cucumbers.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Bologna sausage provides about 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat products are rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sausage contains vitamins B1, B2, B6 and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cream cheese adds calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Dietary fiber from vegetables
items.content: Lettuce and tomato provide a modest amount of fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed meats often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Both the cheese and the sausage contain saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cream cheese can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some Bologna sausages contain nitrites and other preservatives, so moderate consumption is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the Bologna thinly, spread cream cheese on both sides of the bread, add lettuce and a tomato slice. Optionally spread mustard or mayonnaise. The sandwich is easy to eat by hand; you may cut it in half for serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in the refrigerator in an airtight container for no more than 24 hours. Keep the sausage and cheese separately at 2‑4 °C. For longer storage, keep ingredients separate and assemble the sandwich just before serving.
